rulings.reason: The instruction scores the presence and legibility of pun mechanics and stops there -- a judge is told to reward a 'clearly spottable' pun, never whether the wordplay lands, so a caption can max this scale and still be a weak entry. Pun facility does travel with genuine comic skill, so it is mixed.

It credits the surface presence of a name, in-group term, or verbal tic rather than whether the characterization actually works, so a high score certifies a stylistic device rather than quality. Real voice-craft plausibly produces those same markers, so mixed.

The text explicitly forbids scoring funniness and measures only how much of the gag is offloaded onto the unseen drawing, which is a fact about where the joke's information sits -- and about the text-only judging apparatus -- not about the entry's merit. Caption-image interdependence is nonetheless a real contest skill, so mixed.

Both poles are described neutrally with no better end declared, making this a presentation-style axis (scaffolded versus compressed phrasing) rather than an evaluation of the joke. The compression choice plausibly reflects genuine comic judgment, so mixed.

It scores discourse position -- later beat of an exchange versus opening line -- with no good pole stated, so a high score reports a structural convention rather than caption quality. In medias res is often a deliberate craft move, so mixed.

This is a pure subject-matter marker: it scores how far the humor rests on death, injury, or loss while never evaluating whether the dark content is handled well, and the proposer's own examples place the device on both sides of the disagreement. Topic choice by itself is not evidence of craft, so not mixed.
